item.title: Version 1.4.0
item.description:
SupaSidebar 1.4.0

SupaSidebar 1.4.0 makes the sidebar feel more like Arc’s. Let Spaces follow the browser window you’re using, step back and forward through your recent tabs, see which saved link is the tab you’re on, and arrange the top bar your way.

What’s New

  • Back and Forward Through Tabs - New top bar arrows step through the tabs you used recently, in any browser, and right-click lists them.
  • Back and Forward Shortcuts - Set optional shortcuts to go back or forward a tab, across every browser or within the current Space.
  • Show Open Tabs in Saved - A saved link now lights up while its page is your current tab, like a pinned tab in Arc.
  • Hide Saved Tabs From Live Tabs - With Show Open Tabs in Saved on, open tabs that match a saved link can show only in Saved.
  • Customizable Top Bar - Drag buttons to add, remove or reorder them in Settings > Appearance > Top Bar, or right-click the top bar.
  • Duplicate Tab - Right-click an open tab to open a second copy of it in the same browser.
  • Middle-Click to Close Tabs - Middle-click a tab in Live Tabs, in the sidebar or compact mode, to close it.
  • Search Shortcuts for Live Tabs and Saved - Two new shortcuts open the command panel straight into Live Tabs or Saved search.

Improvements

  • Spaces Follow Your Browser Window - With Switch automatically on, focusing a window from a linked profile now switches to its Space.
  • See Why a Space Switched - A short note in the sidebar names the window that caused an automatic switch, with a Stop switching button.
  • Spaces Offer to Switch - Focusing a window from another Space’s linked profile now asks to switch, unless you picked a different behavior.
  • Automatic Switching When You Link a Profile - Linking a browser profile to a Space now turns on Switch automatically if you hadn’t chosen a behavior.
  • Compact Mode Catches Up - Compact mode now highlights your current tab, follows each Space’s linked profile in Live Tabs, and shows switch notes.
  • ⌘N or ⌘T in Your Browser - Pick ⌘N or ⌘T to open the Command Panel inside your browser, with ⌘N as the new default.
  • Tidier ⋯ Menu - The sidebar’s ⋯ menu now groups settings under headings, and holds Full Screen Browser plus any buttons that don’t fit.
  • Updated Onboarding - New users get a simpler first-run setup that brings over their Arc Spaces and pinned tabs.

Bug Fixes

  • Automatic Space switches now leave your browser windows where they are instead of raising or moving them.

Notes

  • Selection Mode is no longer in the ⋯ menu. Start it with right-click > Select, or Shift-click and Command-Shift-click rows.

item.title: Version 1.1.0-beta.2
item.description:
SupaSidebar 1.1.0-beta.2

What’s New

  • Updated Onboarding: New setups now use a browser-aware flow that helps you choose useful sites, configure how SupaSidebar opens, and reach your first working sidebar faster.
  • Search Settings: Find preferences from one search field, jump directly to the right section, and change supported toggles from the results.
  • Scoped Search Shortcuts: Assign optional shortcuts that open the Command Panel directly in the Live Tabs or Saved scope.
  • Precise Auto-Close Duration: Choose a custom timeout using any combination of days, hours, and minutes.
  • Local Folder Preview Sorting: Order files and subfolders by Name A-Z, Name Z-A, Date Modified Newest, or Date Modified Oldest. Name sorting handles numbered files naturally, so Export 2 appears before Export 10.

Improvements

  • Smart Attach Stays in Sync: The menu and Preferences now agree with the sidebar’s actual attachment mode.
  • Sidebar Size and Position Are Remembered: A sidebar you move or resize returns to the same position and height after relaunching SupaSidebar.
  • Auto-Show Is Opt-In for New Setups: The sidebar does not appear automatically when you focus a browser unless you enable Auto Show on Browser Focus.
  • Command Panel shortcut hints now adapt better when the panel has limited space.

Bug Fixes

  • Live Tabs search no longer hides an open tab when the same URL is also saved in SupaSidebar.
  • Dragging a link or folder into a folder no longer moves the entire sidebar window.

Notes

  • Local Folder Preview Sorting applies to Finder-style folder preview columns. It does not rearrange your saved SupaSidebar folders.
